findings.title: Fragments are returned without outer parentheses, so a caller's added AND binds to only part of the OR
findings.body: The org/team authorization fragments come out as `(A) OR (B)` (lines 171-174, 204-207). The eventType filter also comes out unwrapped: `("eventTypeId" = x) OR ("eventParentId" = x)` (line 106). `getBaseConditions` returns the auth fragment as is (line 75), and `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` are public. The point of this refactor is that callers splice the fragment into raw SQL. A caller that writes `WHERE ${base} AND "createdAt" >= ${start}` gets `(A) OR (B) AND createdAt >= …`, which SQL reads as `A OR (B AND …)`. Every team booking then skips the caller's date/status filter, the numbers come out wrong, and nothing reports an error. No caller exists yet, but this is the contract the next PR will build on. Fix: wrap every fragment the class returns, e.g. ``Prisma.sql`(${...})` ``, in the reduce results and in line 106.

findings.title: Unreachable branches in getBaseConditions
findings.body: `getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a `Prisma.Sql` object, which is always truthy (it falls back to `NOTHING_CONDITION`, never null). Because of that, the `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run. Simplify to: `filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${auth}) AND (${filter})` : auth`.

findings.title: Looser public options type hides a missing teamId until runtime
findings.body: The constructor used to accept the discriminated union, so `{ scope: "team" }` without `teamId` failed to compile. With `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions`, that call compiles. The zod parse at line 62 then fails, `options` becomes null, and the service quietly returns `1=0` (no data) with no error. Keep the union type for the constructor, or log or throw when validation fails.

findings.title: Caching tests removed while the caching code remains
findings.body: The `Caching` describe block was deleted, but `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` still cache their results (insightsBooking.ts:83-95). No test covers that behaviour now. The `getBaseConditions` test also covers only the user scope. No test runs an org- or team-scope fragment against the database, which is where the `ANY(${array})` binding and OR precedence matter.

contracts.action: Replace findMany with getBaseConditions returning a Prisma.Sql WHERE fragment
contracts.equivalent_path: Removed findMany, which merged the auth and filter conditions under a Prisma `AND` array
contracts.before_after: Before: the conditions were Prisma where-input objects combined with AND. After: raw SQL fragments. The auth fragment is returned without outer parentheses.
contracts.visible_effect: No production caller in the repository. Only the integration test uses it, via $queryRaw.
contracts.failure_mode: If a caller appends `AND ...` to the fragment, it binds to only the last OR branch and returns wrong rows with no error.

summary: This PR changes InsightsBookingService to return Prisma.sql fragments in place of Prisma where-objects. It removes findMany (nothing in the repository calls it) and rewrites the tests to match. The SQL is equivalent to the old filters. The main problem is that the returned OR fragments have no outer parentheses: once a caller appends its own `AND`, operator precedence quietly drops that condition for some rows. Smaller issues: unreachable branches in getBaseConditions, a looser constructor type that turns a missing teamId into an empty result at runtime, and the deleted caching tests.
